pr.title: Add `-Z hint-mostly-unused` to tell rustc that most of a crate will go unused
pr.description:
This hint allows the compiler to optimize its operation based on this assumption, in order to compile faster. This is a hint, and does not guarantee any particular behavior.

This option can substantially speed up compilation if applied to a large dependency where the majority of the dependency does not get used. This flag may slow down compilation in other cases.

Currently, this option makes the compiler defer as much code generation as possible from functions in the crate, until later crates invoke those functions. Functions that never get invoked will never have code generated for them. For instance, if a crate provides thousands of functions, but only a few of them will get called, this flag will result in the compiler only doing code generation for the called functions. (This uses the same mechanisms as cross-crate inlining of functions.) This does not affect `extern` functions, or functions marked as `#[inline(never)]`.

This option has already existed in nightly as `-Zcross-crate-inline-threshold=always` for some time, and has gotten testing in that form. However, this option is still unstable, to give an opportunity for wider testing in this form.

Some performance numbers, based on a crate with many dependencies having just *one* large dependency set to `-Z hint-mostly-unused` (using Cargo's `profile-rustflags` option):

A release build went from 4m07s to 2m04s.
    
A non-release build went from 2m26s to 1m28s.
pr.author: joshtriplett

classification.name: Inline
evidence: The PR changes `cross_crate_inlinable`, which the concrete MIR `Inline` pass consumes when selecting its inlining cost threshold. The codegen-deferral effect is query/backend behavior, not a separate MirPass, so only `Inline` is assigned.

analysis.summary: Adds a tracked `-Z hint-mostly-unused` option that makes the MIR `Inline` pass treat crate-local functions as cross-crate inlinable so codegen can be deferred until callers reference them. This is a compile-time optimization, not a confirmed bug fix; the flag is explicitly a hint and is intentionally placed after the `#[inline(never)]` rejection so that rejection still wins.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the PR, `cross_crate_inlinable` decides eligibility by first honoring `#[inline(never)]`/availability rejections, then examining the function signature: `let sig = tcx.fn_sig(def_id).instantiate_identity();` and iterating over `sig.inputs()` plus the output to reject signatures whose types are not cross-crate inlinable. There is no crate-wide "mostly unused" shortcut, so a function whose signature fails those type checks is not considered cross-crate inlinable and therefore gets normal local codegen.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation is the optimization introduced by this PR, not a bug fix: after the existing early rejections (including the `#[inline(never)]` check) but before the signature-type loop, it inserts `if tcx.sess.opts.unstable_opts.hint_mostly_unused { return true; }`. Thus for the same crate compiled with `-Z hint-mostly-unused`, functions that were previously rejected by the signature-type checks in `cross_crate_inlinable` now return `true` and can have codegen deferred to referencing crates. The transformation deliberately does not move the flag check before the `#[inline(never)]` rejection, and per the documentation it does not affect `extern` functions or functions marked `#[inline(never)]`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust crate source compiled as a dependency, compared in two configurations that differ only by the presence of `-Z hint-mostly-unused`. The crate should contain: (1) at least one ordinary function that is never called by a downstream crate, (2) at least one ordinary function that is called by a downstream crate, and optionally (3) functions whose signatures would normally be rejected by `cross_crate_inlinable`'s signature-type loop, plus (4) `#[inline(never)]` and `extern` functions as control cases. Downstream code should link the dependency and call/observe the selected functions.
analysis.trigger: Compiling a crate with the unstable option `-Z hint-mostly-unused` set to true, so `tcx.sess.opts.unstable_opts.hint_mostly_unused` is true during `cross_crate_inlinable` evaluation.
preconditions: The crate is compiled with `-Z hint-mostly-unused` (tracked option `hint_mostly_unused: bool = (false, parse_bool, [TRACKED], ...)`).
The function has already passed the pre-existing `#[inline(never)]`/availability rejection checks, because the new return is intentionally after them.
The function is not an `extern` function or otherwise excluded by pre-existing rules, since the documentation states the flag does not affect those.
Downstream crates must invoke the function for it to be code-generated under the deferred-codegen model.
pitfalls: Do not treat the flag as a hard guarantee: documentation says it is a hint and 'does not guarantee any particular behavior'.
Do not expect `#[inline(never)]` functions to be deferred; the check for `inline(never)` precedes the new early return so 'inline(never) wins'.
Do not expect `extern` functions to be affected; the documentation explicitly excludes them.
Do not place the hint check before the `#[inline(never)]`/availability rejection, or those rejections would be overridden.
The option is TRACKED and must be included in tracking-hash tests; the patch adds `tracked!(hint_mostly_unused, true);`.
The flag can slow compilation in cases where most of the crate is actually used, so a runtime/performance test should not assume universal speedup.

Because the early return bypasses the signature-type loop, previously non-cross-crate-inlinable signatures may now be deferred; do not use the old signature-based rejection as the expected result when the flag is on.
analysis.testStrategy: Compile the same dependency crate and downstream caller twice, changing only the presence of `-Z hint-mostly-unused`. First verify both builds succeed and all called functions produce identical runtime results. Then inspect emitted object/symbol output (e.g. `--emit=obj` plus `nm`, or equivalent codegen inspection) for the dependency: with the flag, an uncalled ordinary function that is deferred should be absent or unreferenced in the dependency's generated code, while the downstream-called function must still be present/usable after linking. Include `#[inline(never)]` and `extern` control functions and verify they are still code-generated as before. Also run the interface test that checks unstable tracking hashes and assert `hint_mostly_unused` is tracked. Do not assert exact object contents beyond the documented behavior; the flag is only a hint.
